vulnerability.name: Debug Information Exposure
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities exposing sensitive debugging information in production environments
vulnerability.impact: Information disclosure, internal system exposure, or aid in further attacks
vulnerability.mitigation: Disable debug modes in production, remove development code, implement proper error handling

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: Debugging information is exposed through the use of 'require' statement, which includes a stack trace. In this specific case, the call to the msg.sender.call.value() function will disclose that it is calling a contract function.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
    1. Call withdraw(uint)
    2. Check if credit[msg.sender] is greater than or equal to the provided amount.
    3. Decrease the credit value of msg.sender by the amount.
    4. Call require(msg.sender.call.value(amount)()).
    ```
exploitation_steps: Call withdraw function with an arbitrary amount
findings.exploitation_conditions: An attacker should have a means to call the 'withdraw' function.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary debugging statements like 'require(msg.sender.call.value(amount)())' in production.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The contract is comparing msg.sender with the owner variable, exposing the caller's address in production.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
start -> sendTo -> require(msg.sender == owner) -> expose address
```
exploitation_steps: Call the sendTo function with any valid receiver and amount
findings.remediation: Replace msg.sender with owner before comparing.
